title: Marimo and generic render_visual
description:
It doesn't look like marimo is going to provide functionality like that provided in Jupyter based on this [issue](https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo/issues/9320#issuecomment-4356556270). The suggest using `chart = ggsql.render_altair(table, "VISUALISE x, y DRAW point")`.

My concern is that your blog post suggests you will provide different render methods. I wonder if there could be a more generic render method, like `.render_visual()`, that takes options for a default renderer, making my code a little more robust moving forward.

Super excited about ggsql. Thanks for the work.

title: Issue with columns that have a period in their name
description:
If you use a column with a "." in its name, ggsql (at least the Python interface) fails to render.  Expected behavior was the same DuckDB quoting to work in ggsql. 

(I'm sure not very common, but I was testing it out with some old dataset from R where it often fills in spaces, etc, with periods, and stumbled upon.)

Here's a minimal example:

```
import duckdb
import ggsql
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"numbers": [1,2], "variable": [3,4], "variable.dotted": [3, 4]})
with duckdb.connect("reproduce.db") as con:
    con.sql("CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE test AS SELECT * FROM df")

reader = ggsql.DuckDBReader("duckdb://reproduce.db")

## This works fine:

viz_query = """
SELECT * FROM test
VISUALIZE numbers AS x, variable AS y
DRAW line
LABEL title => 'variable ~ numbers'
"""
viz = reader.execute(viz_query)

writer = ggsql.VegaLiteWriter()
vegalite_json = writer.render(viz)

## This DOES NOT work:

### Show you can query it in DuckDB:

with duckdb.connect("reproduce.db") as con:
    print(con.sql("SELECT \"variable.dotted\" FROM test"))

### But not using the same syntax with ggsql
viz_query = """
SELECT * FROM test
VISUALIZE numbers AS x, "variable.dotted" AS y
DRAW line
LABEL title => 'variable ~ numbers'
"""
viz = reader.execute(viz_query)

writer = ggsql.VegaLiteWriter()
vegalite_json = writer.render(viz) # errors
```
